_description: Single source of truth for CSV column definitions. Both backend generate_synthetic_customer_data.py and load-driver csv_generator.py MUST use these exact column names. The onboarding API (onboarding_api_v2_config_aware.py) validates against these.
_consolidation_note: Consolidated from 15 to 11 files. Primary onboarding: account_details.csv (enriched) + kpi_measurements.csv. Context graph CSVs optional. accounts.csv accepted as backward-compat alias for account_details.csv.

regular_model._description: 2 primary CSVs for onboarding. account_details.csv consolidates accounts + products + stakeholder metadata + business profiles into one file.

account_details.csv.note: Enriched account file. 'products' is a JSON array: [{"name": "...", "category": "...", "arr": 1000000, "use_case": "..."}]. 'use_cases' is a JSON array of what the customer bought us for — strings or {name, product, status: planned|live|at_risk, owner, target_date}; it is read by the extractor (context), the journey/portfolio header, the narrative and Ask AI. 'account_status': active|onboarding|at_risk|churned|paused. Installed-base / once-sold accounts: purchase_date, refresh_date, contract_value (one-time), contract_type (subscription|perpetual|hardware|maintenance) — renewal_date may then carry the refresh date. Trimmed 2026-09-05: a named column exists only when something reads it; everything else goes in 'attributes'. Supersedes accounts.csv + products.csv + account_business_profiles.csv.

accounts.csv.note: arr and renewal_date are required — ROI engine, NRR forecast, and Power-of-1 depend on them.

kpi_measurements.csv.note: Required: source_account_id, kpi_code (a code in the vertical catalog), measured_at, value. pillar / target / weight / status are CATALOG-OWNED: accepted for convenience and ignored by scoring — the catalog version stamped on each health row is the source of truth; a target that disagrees with the catalog is warned at upload. A blank value is a missing measurement (skipped and counted), never 0. NEVER use kpi_data.csv — always kpi_measurements.csv.

enhanced_qualitative_signals.csv.signal_type_vocabulary: the tenant's taxonomy (config/taxonomy_base.json + the vertical overlay) — validated at upload against it; an unknown or blank signal_type is not an error: the row goes to the extractor, which types it from 'content'
enhanced_qualitative_signals.csv.note: The structured lane INTO the signal engine (signals-first, 2026-09-05). A typed row and a raw communication are one contract: the row is 'typed' when signal_type is a taxonomy subtype (no model call), otherwise its content is extracted like any free text. source_platform = the system it came from (salesforce, gainsight, zendesk…); source_ref = that system's id (re-uploads are 'exists', not copies); source_type = email|slack|ticket|transcript|meeting|crm_activity|manual|external (defaults to csv_import). sentiment is NOT required — the engine derives the label from the role and sentiment_score. Money and decisions belong in outcomes.csv, not here. Also accepted as 'signals.csv'; communications.jsonl is the same contract in JSON-lines.

context_graph_model._note: Each file type is defined once, under the section that names its origin (customer_provided / auto_generated / platform_curated). A flat duplicate "files" block was removed 2026-09-01: it shadowed these entries in utils/csv_upload.py's registry, silently dropping the per-section notes and flags and any column added here.
context_graph_model._description: 7 CSVs for context graph mode. 4 customer-provided + 3 auto-generated by platform.

account_business_profiles.csv.note: Merged with old profiles.csv — CSM/champion fields are now optional columns here.

outcomes.csv.outcome_type_vocabulary: the tenant taxonomy's revenue_buckets (protected | expansion | pipeline | at_risk | lost) — validated at upload against them (warning); a row with an unknown type is still stored, with no direction, and is listed on the review surface
outcomes.csv.revenue_sign: revenue is a MAGNITUDE; the bucket gives the sign (lost / at_risk are stored negative). A signed value is accepted; when its sign disagrees with the bucket the row is normalised and warned.
outcomes.csv.db_table: context_nodes (node_type=OUTCOME) via journeys.outcomes.log_outcome — the same lane as the log_outcome tool
outcomes.csv.note: The decision record the measurement chain hangs on: renewal, contraction, churn, expansion, refresh. occurred_at is the DECISION date. source_ref = the order form / opportunity / invoice id (re-uploads are 'exists', not copies). linked_signal_refs: one or several signal refs separated by ';' (their source_ref, our signal id, or node id) — LED_TO edges; left blank when nobody knows, Hindsight derives the association. Installed-base types: refresh_won, repeat_order, maintenance_renewed, attach, refresh_lost, support_lapsed, decommissioned, refresh_at_risk. 'confidence' is accepted and ignored (the unearned-confidence clamp decides).

auto_generated._description: These 2 files are derived by the platform during process-data. If a customer uploads them, the upload is accepted and auto-generation is skipped.

decisions.csv.source: Inferred from story arc patterns + outcome/stakeholder data

signal_edges.csv.source: Derived from temporal correlation between signals + story arc causal chains. Also includes SOURCED_FROM edges (merged from old decision_evidence.csv).

platform_curated._description: Seeded from config/industry_benchmarks/{vertical}.csv. LLM-generated initial data, curated by domain experts. Customer can override by uploading their own.

industry_benchmarks.csv.source: LLM-seeded from industry research (Uptime Institute, ITIC, Gartner, MLPerf, etc.), then curated by domain experts. curated=true means expert-reviewed.

_deprecated._note: These files are no longer generated or requested. The ingestion pipeline accepts them with a deprecation warning for backward compatibility.
_deprecated.customers.csv: Removed — customer record created by /api/onboarding/complete before CSV upload
_deprecated.accounts.csv: Superseded by account_details.csv. Still accepted as backward-compat alias.
_deprecated.products.csv: Absorbed into account_details.csv 'products' JSON column. Standalone upload still accepted.
_deprecated.account_business_profiles.csv: Absorbed into account_details.csv optional columns. Standalone upload still accepted.

_customer_extensions: Every file accepts an optional 'attributes' column (a JSON object) and any UNKNOWN column is folded into attributes.<column> at ingest (warned at upload, never dropped). Attributes are stored on the object (account profile, KPI row, evidence node, outcome node), shown on the surfaces that display it, never scored and never sent to the model or a webhook unless promoted. Promotion / renames: the per-tenant column map (configure_column_map) renames a customer column to one of ours at upload. Rows whose attributes exceed attributes_max_bytes are rejected with a message.
